engagement_background.objective: Cascade Residential Services engaged Treya Partners to capture $870K–$1.7M in annual cost savings (≈$1.3M expected) across key goods and services, boost enterprise value by roughly $16.6 M, and establish a best-in-class, enterprise-wide procurement process that leverages the company’s consolidated buying power.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Initial scope covers nine indirect/direct-indirect spend categories totaling $32.9 M in baseline spend, of which $26.5 M (≈80%) is considered addressable: HVACR OEM/Distributors, HVACR & Plumbing Supplies, Advertising, General Industrial/Electrical Supplies, Electronic Payment Processing, Telecom, Fleet, Uniforms, and Commercial Print. Low-value categories may be dropped after review; no other categories are in scope.
constraints_challenges: Highly decentralized purchasing across multiple operating brands, making aggregation and compliance difficult.
Supplier data gaps – detailed line-item usage often not held internally; requires supplier cooperation which may be slow or unresponsive.
Tight 5–6 month timeline driven by private-equity value-creation targets.
Potential stakeholder pushback or limited availability for data provision, reviews, and negotiations.
Incumbent supplier sensitivities and risk of unsanctioned ‘side conversations’ that could weaken negotiation leverage.

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12 months of AP data (Jan–Dec 2024) is available; contract files and granular usage data must be gathered from individual business units and suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No centralized contract repository; internal systems lack SKU-level detail, and some tail spend may not be addressable, necessitating external supplier data pulls.
